claim_boundary: These entries are research hypotheses. None is a proof, a novelty claim, or evidence that P equals NP.

hypotheses.title: Polynomial Separator Lift Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist universal constants c and k and a deterministic algorithm L running in time N^k such that, for every CNF formula F of encoding length N, L(F) outputs an equisatisfiable CNF formula F' of encoding length at most N^k whose primal graph has treewidth at most c log_2 N. If F' is satisfiable, a satisfying assignment of F can be recovered from a satisfying assignment of F' in time N^k.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Dynamic programming over a width-O(log N) tree decomposition would decide CNF-SAT in polynomial time, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: An infinite CNF family for which every polynomial-size equisatisfiable extension with polynomial-time witness recovery has primal treewidth omega(log N).
A theorem showing that existence of the stated lift contradicts an unconditional representation or extension-complexity lower bound.
attack_surface: CNFs with known treewidth lower bounds
hypotheses.claim_boundary: As stated, the unrestricted polynomial-time transformer permits the solve-and-encode construction if P = NP. H001 is therefore theorem-equivalent to P = NP rather than an independently specified mechanism. Its useful descendant must restrict the transformation model.

hypotheses.title: Exact Submodular Lift Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist a universal constant k and a deterministic polynomial-time transformation S that maps every CNF formula F of encoding length N to an explicitly represented submodular function g_F: {0,1}^m -> Q with m <= N^k, polynomial-bit rational values, and polynomial-time evaluation, such that min g_F = 0 if and only if F is satisfiable. From every zero-valued minimizer, a satisfying assignment of F is recoverable in polynomial time.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Polynomial-time submodular minimization would decide CNF-SAT, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: A representation lower bound proving that some CNF family requires superpolynomial m, coefficient length, or evaluation-circuit size for every exact submodular lift satisfying the recovery condition.
A structural invariant preserved by submodular lifts but violated by the satisfying-assignment relation of an explicit CNF family.
attack_surface: cut and correlation polytope lower bounds
hypotheses.claim_boundary: As stated, the unrestricted polynomial-time transformer permits the solve-and-encode construction if P = NP. H002 is theorem-equivalent to P = NP and does not yet isolate a non-circular submodular mechanism.

hypotheses.title: Totally Unimodular Feasibility Lift Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist a universal constant k and a deterministic algorithm T running in time N^k that maps every CNF formula F of encoding length N to a rational linear system A_F z <= b_F of total encoding length at most N^k, where A_F is totally unimodular, such that the system is feasible if and only if F is satisfiable. From a feasible point, a satisfying Boolean assignment of F is recoverable in time N^k.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Linear programming would decide CNF-SAT in polynomial time, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: An unconditional lower bound ruling out every polynomial-size totally unimodular nonemptiness-preserving formulation with polynomial-time witness recovery for an explicit CNF family.
A proof that the recovery requirement forces a known polytope with superpolynomial extension complexity to appear as a projection or face.
attack_surface: cut, stable-set, and correlation polytope extension complexity
nonemptiness-only formulations versus full convex-hull formulations
hypotheses.claim_boundary: As stated, the unrestricted polynomial-time transformer permits the solve-and-encode construction if P = NP. Polytope extension lower bounds remain relevant only after a restricted lift class is fixed.

hypotheses.title: Constant-Level Exact Moment Lift Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist universal constants d and k and a deterministic polynomial-time transformation M that maps every CNF formula F of encoding length N to a polynomial system P_F with at most N^k variables, constraints, degree, and coefficient bit-length, such that the degree-2d sum-of-squares moment relaxation of P_F is feasible if and only if F is satisfiable, and a satisfying assignment of F can be recovered in polynomial time from every feasible relaxation solution.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: A constant-level semidefinite program of polynomial size would decide CNF-SAT, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: An integrality-gap theorem that survives every polynomial-size, polynomial-degree auxiliary-variable lift satisfying the stated witness-recovery condition.
A lower bound proving that d must grow without bound for an explicit family under the exact transformation model.
attack_surface: Tseitin and random CSP integrality gaps
hypotheses.claim_boundary: As stated, the unrestricted polynomial-time transformer permits solve-and-encode if P = NP. Direct hierarchy gaps do not refute it, but the statement is not yet a mechanism independent of the target theorem.

hypotheses.title: Unrestricted Dag-like Res(⊕) Lower-Bound Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exists an explicit polynomial-time constructible family {F_n} of unsatisfiable CNF formulas of size poly(n) such that every unrestricted dag-like Resolution-over-Parities, Res(⊕), refutation of F_n has size n^{omega(1)}.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: This would give the first superpolynomial size lower bound for unrestricted dag-like Res(⊕), a proof system strictly stronger than ordinary resolution and a natural fragment of AC^0[2]-Frege. It would not by itself resolve P versus NP.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial-size unrestricted dag-like Res(⊕) refutation family for every explicit candidate family covered by the exact statement.
A theorem proving that every unsatisfiable CNF has polynomial-size dag-like Res(⊕) refutations.
attack_surface: possible polynomial upper bounds using unrestricted reuse
hypotheses.claim_boundary: Current cited results cover regular or depth-restricted fragments and explicitly leave unrestricted dag-like size lower bounds open. OPEN records only that this literature audit did not settle the conjecture.

hypotheses.title: Extended Frege Superpolynomial Lower-Bound Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exists an explicit polynomial-time constructible family {T_n} of propositional tautologies of size poly(n) such that every Extended Frege proof of T_n has size n^{omega(1)}.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: This would establish a superpolynomial lower bound for one of the strongest standard propositional proof systems and would be a major advance in proof complexity. It would not automatically settle P versus NP.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial p such that every propositional tautology of length n has an Extended Frege proof of size at most p(n).
Polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs for the exact explicit family named by any sharpened descendant of this hypothesis.
attack_surface: known lower bounds only for restricted Frege systems
connections between Extended Frege, bounded arithmetic, and circuit lower bounds
hypotheses.claim_boundary: No explicit candidate family is selected yet, so H006 is a frontier statement rather than a publishable new conjecture. It is mutually incompatible with H011.

hypotheses.title: Full IPS Lower Bound for Explicit CNF Conjecture over GF(2)
hypotheses.statement: There exists an explicit polynomial-time constructible family {F_n} of unsatisfiable CNF formulas of size poly(n) such that every unrestricted Ideal Proof System refutation of the standard Boolean polynomial encoding of F_n over GF(2) has algebraic-circuit size n^{omega(1)}.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: This would extend lower bounds from restricted IPS fragments to full IPS on Boolean CNF instances and would connect propositional proof complexity to major algebraic circuit lower-bound questions.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial upper bound on full IPS refutation size for every unsatisfiable Boolean CNF over GF(2).
Polynomial-size full IPS refutations for the exact explicit family selected by a sharpened descendant.
attack_surface: roABP-IPS and multilinear IPS lower bounds
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The cited 2025-2026 results prove lower bounds for restricted IPS fragments, not unrestricted full IPS. H007 makes no novelty claim and does not assert a particular hard family.

hypotheses.title: AC^0[2]-Frege Superpolynomial Lower-Bound Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exists an explicit polynomial-time constructible family {T_n} of propositional tautologies of size poly(n) such that every AC^0[2]-Frege proof of T_n has size n^{omega(1)}.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: This would resolve a central open problem in bounded-depth proof complexity and separate a substantially stronger system than resolution. It would not alone prove P != NP.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial p such that every tautology has an AC^0[2]-Frege proof of size at most p(n).
Polynomial-size AC^0[2]-Frege proofs for the exact explicit family selected by a sharpened descendant.
attack_surface: Res(⊕) lower bounds as fragment evidence
hypotheses.claim_boundary: Known lower bounds for Res(⊕), regular systems, tree-like Frege, or restricted IPS do not automatically imply AC^0[2]-Frege lower bounds.

hypotheses.title: Bounded-Radius Definitional Treewidth Compiler Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist constants r, c, and k and a finite ordered set R of syntactic CNF rewrite rules with the following properties. Each rule inspects a connected incidence subformula containing at most r clauses and r current variables; introduces at most r fresh variables constrained only by fan-in-two Tseitin definitional equivalences; and deletes or replaces clauses only when equivalence of the affected fragment relative to at most r boundary variables is certified by an exhaustive local truth table. The deterministic compiler applies the first applicable rule in canonical lexicographic order for at most N^k steps. For every input CNF F of encoding length N, the compiler halts with an equisatisfiable CNF F_R of length at most N^k and primal treewidth at most c log_2 N, and a satisfying assignment of F is recoverable by reversing the committed local certificates in time N^k.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The fixed local compiler followed by bounded-treewidth dynamic programming would decide CNF-SAT in polynomial time, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: A theorem that every finite bounded-radius rule system of the stated kind fails to reduce some explicit CNF family to O(log N) primal treewidth within polynomially many steps.
For any proposed concrete rule set R, an explicit formula family or finite counterexample violating equivalence, size, termination, treewidth, or witness recovery.
attack_surface: minor and separator invariants under local extensions
local truth-table certificates versus global structure
hypotheses.claim_boundary: Unlike H001, H009 forbids an unrestricted transformer from first solving SAT: all semantic work is confined to constant-radius truth-table certificates and a fixed finite rule set. No such rule set is currently known.

hypotheses.title: Bounded-Degree Extended Polynomial Calculus Automatization Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist constants d and k and a fixed deterministic algorithm A over GF(2) such that, on every CNF formula F of encoding length N, A uses only Boolean polynomial-calculus inference, multilinear reduction, and fan-in-two extension axioms of the forms y = uv, y = u + v, and y = 1 - u; keeps every stored polynomial at multilinear degree at most d; stores and derives at most N^k total symbols; and within N^k steps outputs either a polynomial-calculus derivation of 1 when F is unsatisfiable or a satisfying Boolean assignment when F is satisfiable.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: A would be a deterministic polynomial-time SAT algorithm, implying P = NP.
falsification_conditions: An explicit CNF family requiring unbounded degree, superpolynomial symbol count, or superpolynomial steps for every fixed algorithm using exactly the allowed inference and extension rules.
A lower-bound theorem for the stated extended system and automatization model, not merely for direct polynomial calculus or a restricted IPS fragment.
attack_surface: Tseitin and random-CNF polynomial-calculus degree lower bounds
extension variables bypassing direct-encoding lower bounds
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The statement specifies a restricted inference language and a fixed automatizer, but it does not provide A. Existing lower bounds for direct polynomial calculus and restricted IPS fragments do not settle this extension-enabled model.

hypotheses.title: Polynomially Bounded Extended Frege Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exists a polynomial p such that every propositional tautology of encoding length n has an Extended Frege proof of size at most p(n).
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Extended Frege would be a polynomially bounded propositional proof system, implying NP = coNP. This implication is weaker than P = NP and does not itself provide an efficient proof-search algorithm.
falsification_conditions: An explicit polynomial-time constructible tautology family requiring n^{omega(1)} Extended Frege proof size.
A superpolynomial Extended Frege lower bound for any explicit family, as asserted by H006.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: H011 and H006 are mutually incompatible, yet neither is currently refuted by the cited literature. Registering both demonstrates that OPEN is not a probability or endorsement.
